sources.title: DINO (computer vision) - AI Wiki
sources.snippet: DINO (self- DI stillation with NO labels) is a family of self-supervised learning methods for computer vision from Meta AI that trains Vision Transformers (ViTs) on unlabeled images and produces general-purpose visual features rivaling or surpassing those learned with human-labeled supervision [1] [2].

sources.snippet: Dino for Classification Overview This repository is a compact, custom PyTorch implementation of Dino for Classification. The small configuration is intended for code review, smoke tests, and small controlled experiments rather than as a production-ready pretrained release.

sources.title: DINO | Model Families | Robots Atlas
sources.snippet: About DINO is a family of self-supervised vision models developed by Meta AI (FAIR). The name stands for "self-DIstillation with NO labels". Successive generations — DINO (2021), DINOv2 (2023) and DINOv3 (2025) — train vision backbones (Vision Transformer, ConvNeXt) without labels, producing general-purpose, high-quality image features useful for classification, detection, segmentation and ...

sources.title: DINO, DINOv2 and DINOv3, Explained for AI Engineers
sources.snippet: DINO turns an image into vectors you can compare, one for the image and one per patch DINO models are vision transformers. A vision transformer, or ViT, cuts the image into small square patches, 14 × 14 pixels for DINOv2 and 16 × 16 for DINOv3, and treats each patch the way a language model treats a word (the transformer article covers how).
